Senior Spotlight: Student Body President Layla Ruesch

October 7, 2026 by Caitlynn Brinkerhoff Leave a Comment

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:35
Instaread

​Layla Ruesch, a White Pine County senior, was born and raised in Ely. “Growing up in a small community has allowed me to build strong connections with my family, friends, school and community,” she said. “I am grateful to have grown up in Ely and for all the experiences that have helped shape who I am today.”

Ruesch is a three-sport athlete, playing volleyball, softball and basketball for all four years of high school. “Being involved in sports has taught me the importance of teamwork, commitment and hard work,” she commented.

Outside of her athletics, Ruesch enjoys being involved in her school and community. She is currently the secretary of the National Honor Society, which she has been a member of since her junior year. Ruesch is also student body president and has served on student council for all four years of high school. At age nine, she found a passion for showing lambs with 4-H, which taught her responsibility and dedication. “Being involved in these activities has given me many opportunities to grow, take on leadership roles and be a part of my school and community.”

Ruesch enjoys working with numbers and solving problems. Her favorite class was math with Mrs. Murphree. “The way she was able to explain and break down tough problems was super beneficial to me and made me enjoy math that much more,” she stated.

High school has continually created memorable moments for Ruesch. “Over the years, I have built memories with many coaches, teammates, teachers and classmates that I will cherish forever. A lot of my favorite memories have come from all of the sports trips that I have been a part of the last four years.”

Ruesch credits her parents as her inspiration; they support and encourage her to keep going while teaching her the importance of working hard and staying true to herself. “Watching everything they do for our family motivates me to become the best version of myself,” she said. “Their strength, love and everything they do for me remind me that I can overcome challenges and achieve my goals. I am grateful for everything they have done for me throughout my life.”

She encourages her classmates not to waste their time, reminding them that, “Once it is over, you can never go back. Time is a precious thing.”

Ruesch plans to attend Boise State University in Idaho after graduation. She is unsure what she will major in but is excited to explore her options, try new things and meet new people. “I am keeping my options open.”
